note:
Measured baselines for the PR gate (EVAL.md section 4). A row is claimed by bench + model + provider + prompt_version; `bun scripts/agent-eval.ts --baseline` fails the run when it drops more than one question below `passed`, hits the turn cap at all, falls below `recall`, or, where the row carries one, lands more than 0.05 under `presentation`. avg_turns is 1 on nearly every claude-code row because that provider owns its own loop: one qwry turn covers the whole conversation, so turns compare only within a provider (EVAL.md section 6). Every Pagila row is transcribed from the run artifact of the same name under eval/results/, `date` included: it is the harness's own `config.date`, so a row can be recomputed from its artifact and nothing else. A row is ONE artifact: where a run was sampled twice, the row is the run and the second sample is evidence about it, not a better version of it. The four staging rows are the exception, and it is stated rather than hidden: their artifacts hold the maintainer's data and never enter the repo (section 2), so those four numbers are transcribed from runs nothing in this repo can re-open or recompute. 

2026-09-06, W3b: every row is now PROMPT_VERSION v4 and the v3 rows committed at d30e28a are superseded. v4 is the v3 string with three SQL rules inserted into the list rule 1 already sits in and nothing else moved, so these rows read against the v3 ones directly. They exist because two v3 rows recorded a loss: section 4 refuses a prompt that trades correctness for prettiness, and v3 had bought presentation (insight 0.514 to 0.850 on Haiku) with SQL. Both losses are recovered. `pagila.json` + claude-sonnet-5 is 33/33 where v3 read 28/33 and v1 read 32/33: t3-08, t4-04 and t5-01 all pass with the extra column gone, and t1-07, the v3 note's sampling-noise row, passes too. `pagila-hard.json` + claude-haiku-4-5 is 5/5 where v3 read 3/5: ph-05 pre-aggregates rental and payment in their own CTEs instead of joining both to customer in one pass, and ph-03 casts to numeric inside the LAG division. Neither fix cost the other model anything: Haiku `pagila.json` holds 33/33 and Sonnet `pagila-hard.json` holds 5/5. Both `pagila.json` rows keep recall 0.94, which is one question, t4-02, whose gold table the prefilter's candidate set misses at v1, v3 and v4 alike; that is prefilter work and it caps this bench below 1.00 for any prompt version. 

One row is worse at v4 than at v3, and it is armed at what was measured rather than at what was wanted. `pagila-insight.json` + claude-haiku-4-5 reads 7/8 ran and presentation 0.714 over 7, where the v3 row carried 8/8 and 0.850 over 8. The accuracy half is one question and inside section 4's tolerance; the presentation half is 0.136 under a rule whose slack is 0.05, so section 4's `presentation never goes down` is NOT MET on this row. Writing 0.714 into it does not make it met and is not meant to: it stops the next Haiku insight run being gated against a number this prompt has never reached, and it leaves the miss on the record where the next wave has to answer it. Nothing here says which of two readings is right, because neither was measured. Sampling variance: this is the first repeat of ANY kind on this bench, so the 0.05 slack has still never been tested, which is exactly what the v3 note said would test it. Or the three SQL rules crowding the answer shape: the circumstantial number is that the run got much heavier, avg_out_tokens 2302.8 to 3438.5, avg_tool_calls 5.5 to 7.1, avg_wall 28.8 s to 57.7 s, avg_turns 1 to 2.5. Like for like over the seven questions both runs scored, v3c reads 0.886 and v4 reads 0.714, and every one of the five checks moved down or stayed; none moved up. The unscored answer is `ins-05`, which EXEC-FAILed twice in a row at v4 (12 model turns and about 225 s each, the model's own final text claiming the database is unresponsive while the lab Postgres answered a count immediately after the run); it also EXEC-FAILed at v3's first draft and ran in one turn at v3c, so it is not new, but twice consecutively is. Telling variance from cause needs a full v4 re-sample and a v3 control, and neither has been run. The Sonnet row moves the other way over the same eight answers, 0.825 to 0.900, with `bullets_in_range` 6/8 to 8/8 and `figure_per_finding` 6/8 to 8/8; `no_grid_restatement` went 6/8 to 5/8 there, so DESIGN rule 14 is still the check that has not landed on either model. 

The four staging rows are new: no staging row existed at any prompt version, so `--baseline` read both staging benches as unmeasured, which is red and not green. Section 4's release gate says the maintainer's staging numbers go into this file, and these are them. `staging.json` is 23/23 on both models, which on Sonnet is +2 over v3 and +1 over the 2026-09-03 reference: s3-04's generate_series calendar spine is gone (12 rows over three months of signups) and s5-02 keeps total_amount inside its ranking CTE, each fixed by the v4 rule written for it. `staging-hard.json` is 5/5 on Sonnet and armed at 4/5 on Haiku, up one from both the v3 row and the 09-03 reference, with h-05 flipped to a pass by the join and cast rules and h-01 still lost: the predicted cohort test has no lower bound, so a user whose first wardrobe product predates their own signup counts as activated. h-01 is not a v4 regression, it failed at the 09-03 reference too, and no v4 rule addresses it. Arming 4/5 accepts 3 on a later run, which is the judgment the pagila-hard Haiku row carried at v3; it is armed anyway because unmeasured is not green. Detail per question, both Pagila and staging: `ROADMAP_log.md`, the W3b note.
